messages:
maria: Quick pulse — I want to propose a small, backwards-compatible change to our token-level metrics so TTFT vs decode vs kernel time are clearer in dashboards. Thinking sampling per-token spans + kernel attribution labels.

oliver: +1. current panels are confusing: the stacked bars look like decode is the whole cost but TTFT is actually dominated by batch wait on p99.

kevin: can you sketch the metric shape? labels, aggregation keys?

maria: sure, rough sketch: use a sampled per-token trace emitted at the end of request (cheap):
```
redwood_token_phase_seconds_total{route="/chat",model="rwi-7b",phase="ttft",phase_stage="prefetch"} 0.00045
redwood_token_phase_seconds_total{route="/chat",model="rwi-7b",phase="decode",kernel="matmul"} 0.0012
redwood_token_phase_seconds_total{route="/chat",model="rwi-7b",phase="kernel",kernel_type="fused_attn"} 0.0009
redwood_token_phase_seconds_total{route="/chat",model="rwi-7b",phase="kv_lookup",kv_cache_hit="true"} 0.00008

# labels: route, model, phase, kernel_type (optional), kv_cache_hit, batch_size, selected_kernel_variant
```

jia: I like the separate phase label. Two questions: (1) how do we avoid cardinality explosion with model+route+kernel_type combos? (2) how to map kernel_time to CUDA kernel timings?

maria: good points. answers: (1) only emit kernel_type and selected_kernel_variant when selection differs from default or when in debug sampling mode; default emission omits kernel_type to keep cardinality low. (2) we can expose kernel_ms from the runtime kernel profiler (aggregated per-request) as a label value or separate metric redwood_kernel_ms{kernel_type=...,device=...}. We'll map the kernel name to a canonical short id during model load.

sam: For KV cache: we must be careful — a KV cache hit reduces decode cost but still costs a small lookup and potential memcpy. Suggest a tiny phase kv_lookup_ms that always exists (usually <0.1ms) and kv_cache_hit boolean label so dashboards can subtract it cleanly.

perf-bot: automated note: recent perf job 2026-02-19 flagged a small p99 TTFT regression on rwi-7b under burst traffic. Attaching run id: perf-20260219-77.

kevin: good call. we should also instrument batch wait separately: redwood_batch_wait_seconds{route=...,batch_size=...,queue_depth=...}. right now batch_wait is implicit in TTFT and hard to attribute.

maria: agreed. Proposed minimal schema (no new timers per-token unless sampled):
1) sampled_token_span: single emitted blob per token sampled with labels [route,model,token_index,batch_size,kv_cache_hit,selected_kernel_variant]
2) counters/gauges: redwood_token_phase_seconds_total{route,model,phase} + redwood_kernel_ms_total{kernel_id,device}
3) batch_wait histogram: redwood_batch_wait_seconds_bucket{le=...,route,model}

oliver: how will dashboards compute per-token p95 decomposition? we'll need to join sampled spans with counters?

maria: dashboards should primarily use the sampled_token_span for percentile decomposition (samples are weighted by sample rate). For aggregate throughput/ cost panels use counters/histograms. Grafana dashboard plan:
- Panel A: stacked percentiles (p50/p95/p99) where each stack is phase: prefetch | kv_lookup | batch_wait | decode | postprocess. Source: sampled_token_span (with sample-rate correction).
- Panel B: kernel attribution heatmap: kernel_id x p95 kernel_ms. Source: redwood_kernel_ms_total / invocations.
- Panel C: route-level KPI: tokens/sec, avg_token_cost, tail_TTFT. Source: counters & billing metrics.

jia: sampling logic? uniform random X% of tokens? Or sample per-request first N tokens?

maria: recommend hybrid: sample first token of each request (captures cold-path: model load, prefix costs) + random 0.1% of subsequent tokens to capture steady-state. Also increase sampling on p99 alert windows.

sam: small nit: be explicit about where kernel selection time shows up. There's the decision time (host CPU) and kernel execution time (device). Decision time should be labeled as phase=kernel_selection_host_ms. We currently fold it into decode.

maria: yep, add kernel_selection_host_ms phase label. Also map memcpy and sync time into kernel_ms_substages if we can get them cheaply.

kevin: implementation note: agent that emits sampled_token_span must be asynchronous and non-blocking. If we do synchronous JSON writes we'll blow tail latency. Use buffered UDP or an in-process ringbuffer flush to statsd/grafana-agent.

perf-bot: suggestion: add a quick nightly job that recomputes per-route p99 decomposition from sampled spans and stores precomputed snapshots for dashboard fast loads.

oliver: agree. Metrics storage could be expensive if we keep raw spans. Precompute and store daily snapshots for last 30 days plus a rolling 24h fast store.

maria: tentative action items: 
- kevin: prototype metric names & low-cardinality label set + example exporter (due EOW)
- sam: add kv_lookup phase and batch_wait histogram in runtime (PR target Wed)
- jia: dashboard mockup (Grafana) with stacked percentile panel (due Thu)
- perf-bot / infra: nightly snapshot job (sync with infra team)

kevin: ack, will start. question: do we need per-route sampling rates? some routes are too heavy.

maria: yes, per-route sampling rate config in console would be ideal. start with per-model/per-route defaults and expose overrides.

oliver: small UX ask: make the kernel_id human-friendly (short alias + underlying long name) in hover tooltip.

maria: will do. ok team, I'll open a RFC doc and a small PR to add the minimal metrics. If anyone wants to review the schema ping me.

sam: thanks. quick follow-up: should we tag samples with request_id so we can rehydrate traces for debugging? even if only in debug mode.

maria: yes, keep request_id on sampled spans only. not on counters.

oliver: great thread. :thumbsup:

maria: ending with one more snippet for console config interface (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
sampling:
  default_token_sample_rate: 0.001 # 0.1%
  per_route_overrides:
    "/chat": 0.002
    "/embedding": 0.0001
```

maria: ok closing — will land RFC + PRs. reviewers: @kevin @sam @jia.
